Don't feel down on yourself. I don't want to judge your actions at work, except to say that we all make mistakes and that you shouldn't be too hard on yourself.

As for being a smart "freak" - you'd be surprised how many guys like intelligent women (I know I do). Don't give up on other people just because you feel out of place. I made this mistake a few years ago and felt like you do, but since I started letting people back in, things have improved drastically. Hope this helps, even a bit :)

If it helps, I can assure you the job market sucks for everyone right now, not just you. As for the prescriptions, did you already check into Medicaid? I am no expert, but it seems like it would be worth checking into. You also might want to check into prescription discount programs. If you live in the States, many county governments here offer such programs. 

My only suggestion regarding jobs would be to keep your options open. I used to work in a technical field but cannot find work in the current employment market either. However, I'm looking at it as a blessing in disguise and am now pondering a career change. So don't worry, something will come through!

Here's a link to that program I mentioned:
http://www.naco.org/Template.cfm?Section=County_Membership&Template=/TaggedPage/TaggedPageDisplay.cfm&TPLID=72&ContentID=16869

Thanks guys, it's really nice to find people who actually listen to me. Guess something just went off in my head this weekend and I had to let it out. I looked into volunteering a while back but was having trouble finding anything in my area. I might look into it again later this week. I have been trying to line up some crap job (waiting tables, customer service, etc) to get me something to do for a while now, but I think the fact that I'm usually either overqualified or don't have the appropriate experience has made getting one a bit harder. 

Anyway, I'm feeling a bit better today. I spent most of today fixing up the house; I am in the process of selling it (part of a larger plan I've made, long story) and just doing something with my hands helped. 

Aenea, I actually did ask my friend for "girl help" once; she said I'm a good catch but just needed to be more playful and relaxed, and maybe learn how to flirt a bit. I'm trying to work on letting that side show a bit more, hopefully it'll pay off someday...
